title: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
hook: A GUI agent framework that treats every finished task as a lesson: it banks the experience into memory and skills, then reuses them across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, and Windows.
key_points: Targets a gap in the OpenClaw agent framework: weak cross-platform GUI interaction and no real self-evolution mechanism.
Introduces a Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework: a host agent decomposes long-horizon tasks using accumulated experience (Know), then routes them to a pluggable GUI subagent.
The GUI subagent pairs an experience-attributable memory system with a self-evolving skill library, letting it migrate across platforms and reuse fast paths (Act).
Continuously stores user profiles and feedback to sharpen task decomposition and tool-call accuracy over time.

With open-source Kimi-2.6 as the base model, reaches 64.1% on the long-horizon MobileWorld benchmark, ahead of other agent frameworks and closed models like Seed-2.0-Pro and GPT-5.5; the memory/skill layer transfers across base models, adding +8.5% with Kimi-2.6.
content_html: OpenClaw has become a go-to framework for automating complex tasks with agents, but the paper points at two real gaps: it struggles across different device GUIs, and it has no solid way to actually get better from experience. KnowAct-GUIClaw is built to close both.
extra_html:
Yunxin Li and colleagues propose a "Know Deeply, Act Perfectly" paradigm: accumulated user interaction and task-running experience should directly sharpen execution accuracy and efficiency, unifying understanding and action rather than treating them separately. Their Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework puts a host agent in charge of long-horizon task decomposition, drawing on accumulated experience and task-relevant knowledge, then routes work to a pluggable GUI subagent. That subagent carries an experience-attributable memory system and a self-evolving skill library, which is what lets it move across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, and Windows without relearning from scratch — and the framework keeps banking user profiles and feedback to keep improving decomposition and tool-call accuracy.

Across all four platforms, the authors report KnowAct-GUIClaw ahead on efficiency, accuracy, and cross-platform adaptability; with the open-source Kimi-2.6 model as its base, it hits 64.1% on the long-horizon MobileWorld benchmark, beating other agent frameworks and closed models including Seed-2.0-Pro and GPT-5.5. They also report the memory-and-skill layer transfers across different base models, adding 8.5% when paired with Kimi-2.6. Li and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: UI-MOPD: Teaching One GUI Agent Many Platforms Without Forgetting
related.hook: Train a GUI agent on a new platform and it often forgets the old ones. UI-MOPD picks a different teacher per platform on the fly, so cross-platform learning stops fighting itself.

related.title: GUI vs. CLI: Where Computer-Use Agents Get Stuck
related.hook: Should an agent click buttons or type commands? A matched benchmark giving both the same 440 tasks finds GUI agents win by default — but CLI agents leap ahead once their skill library is filled in.

flashcards.prompt: What two gaps in the OpenClaw agent framework does KnowAct-GUIClaw target?
flashcards.back_html: Weak cross-platform GUI interaction support, and the lack of a well-built self-evolution mechanism for improving from execution experience.

flashcards.prompt: What does the 'Know-Route-Act-Reflect' framework's host agent do?

choices.text: Uses accumulated interaction experience and task-relevant knowledge to decompose and route long-horizon tasks
Directly executes every low-level GUI click itself, with no subagents
Only handles Windows-platform tasks, delegating everything else

flashcards.explanation_html: The host agent's job is long-horizon task decomposition and allocation, drawing on accumulated experience — the actual GUI manipulation is handled by a pluggable subagent.

flashcards.prompt: How does KnowAct-GUIClaw's GUI subagent support moving to a new platform without starting over?
flashcards.back_html: It pairs an experience-attributable memory system with a self-evolving skill library, enabling cross-platform migration and reuse of fast paths already learned.

flashcards.prompt: What result on the MobileWorld benchmark does the paper highlight for the Kimi-2.6-based GUIClaw?

choices.text: 64.1% task success, ahead of other agent frameworks and closed models like Seed-2.0-Pro and GPT-5.5
100% task success, solving every MobileWorld task
It underperformed closed-source models on MobileWorld

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper reports 64.1% as the best result on the long-horizon MobileWorld benchmark among the agent frameworks and models it compares against.
